sentences.text: Arminisaurus was a plesiosaur about 3 to 4 meters long, known only from a fragmentary skeleton that is roughly 40 percent complete. This remains include an incomplete lower jaw, teeth, vertebrae, and parts of the pectoral girdle and paddles.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was found in the early 1980s by collector Lothar Schulz in the Beukenhorst II clay pit near Bielefeld. The species Arminisaurus schuberti was formally described in 2018 by paleontologists Sven Sachs and Benjamin Kear.
The genus name honors Arminius, a Cherusci chieftain who defeated three Roman legions in 9 AD, while the species name schuberti commemorates amateur paleontologist Siegfried Schubert.

Arminisaurus belongs to the family Pliosauridae, a group of plesiosaurs ranging from the Early Jurassic to the early Late Cretaceous. It is considered a basal pliosaurid, distinguished from other members of its clade by specific characteristics in the mandible, neck vertebrae, and scapula.

This animal lived during the Pliensbachian stage, approximately 192.9 to 184.2 million years ago. Arminisaurus is one of only three plesiosaurian taxa described from the Pliensbachian stage, alongside Westphaliasaurus and Cryonectes.
